1. Case 1: Acute epididymo-orchitis
The 13-year-old boy presents with left scrotal soreness and oedema for five days. Physical examination shows an enlarged testis and epididymis with purulent foci and no torsion. Laboratory tests reveal leukocytosis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa growth, strongly indicating a bacterial infection. Doppler ultrasound shows preserved blood flow and enhanced vascularity, supporting acute epididymo-orchitis while refuting testicular torsion and tumor. Negative urinalysis and occult penis favor a primary scrotal infection. Although a mild whirlpool sign raises minor concern for torsion, preserved perfusion and overwhelming infectious evidence make torsion and tumor unlikely. Thus the diagnosis is acute epididymo-orchitis.
